card: This PR completely reimplements private broadcast by replacing bitcoind internal peer connections with an isolated, node-stateless job runner and standalone CLI tool (bitcoin-privbcast). The new system queries Tor DNS seeds and schedules fixed BIP324 connections over dedicated Tor circuits, eliminating reliance on addrman and internal node state to prevent timing oracles and privacy leaks. It also removes legacy private broadcast code from net and PeerManager and adds 1-parent-1-child package relay support to submitpackage. The change is motivated by repeated privacy leaks in the legacy architecture, including direct connection proxy bypasses and clearnet discouragement oracles. It touches networking, RPC, and package validation across more than 17,000 lines.
evidence: Author cites four prior vulnerabilities and leaks in the existing private broadcast implementation that required careful fixes: proxy bypass during v2->v1 reconnections (#35319/#35410), peer discouragement acting as a clearnet oracle (#36312), mempool inspection leaking completion (#36277), and private broadcast connections writing to addrman (#35032).

Author notes that addrman destinations are inherently attacker-influenced via gossip, making static Tor-resolved DNS seeds necessary to eliminate user-specific and peer-manipulated fingerprints within a release.
problem: The existing private broadcast mechanism relies on node state and addrman for peer selection and retry decisions, creating timing oracles and privacy fingerprint vectors that adversaries can exploit or manipulate via addr gossip. Additionally, the existing relay does not support packages, preventing private broadcast of low-fee transactions that rely on child-pays-for-parent to enter mempools.

risk.why: Flaws in the custom SOCKS5/BIP324 state machine or proxy handling could leak the sender IP address or Tor anonymity, while bugs in the package validation modifications could impact transaction evaluation.

scope_notes: Extremely large patch (+17211/-4442 across 121 files) organized into four distinct parts: common library refactoring, the standalone bitcoin-privbcast binary and specification, bitcoind job queue integration alongside legacy code removal, and package relay (1P1C) support across privbcast, validation, and RPC.
summary: Replaces Bitcoin Core's private broadcast subsystem with an isolated, state-less job runner that discovers IPv4/IPv6 peer targets via Tor DNS seeds and connects using fresh SOCKS5 circuits and BIP324 v2 transport. Extracts transport and BIP324 code into the common library, introduces a standalone bitcoin-privbcast executable, and removes the legacy private broadcast peer connection and relay logic from net and PeerManager. Extends private broadcast to support 1-parent-1-child package relay via submitpackage and ProcessNewPackage test evaluations.
uncertainties: Diff was omitted, so validation adjustments in ProcessNewPackage and specific low-level socket handling cannot be independently verified.
